findings.passage: The test going forward is simple. If he starts choosing recognition over fun when the two split, the case for Three gets stronger.
findings.problem: This is the page's only stated mechanism for revisiting a contested, medium-confidence typing, and nothing tracks it. No claim in evidence-draft.json carries this passage or a review_trigger for the type read. type_hypothesis.discriminator mentions it only as prose. The test also names no observable split, so a 2030 refresh cannot tell whether it fired. The record already holds the catalysts most likely to settle 7 vs 3 within five years: the Hollywood leap he named as the goal in June 2026 (S16, "all I want to do is make TV and films in Hollywood"), the next Emmy cycle after the YouTube-backed 2026 campaign (C110), any public account of how he took the September 2026 loss (C109; the record has none), and whether Keep the Meter Running stays self-funded. That last one is the costly choice the Seven case rests on at "What gives the line weight is what it costs him" (C34, C95), and those triggers are written as fact updates, not as a test of the argument.
findings.acceptance_test: The prose names at least one concrete, observable split in reader language. Example: if a TV, film or streaming deal arrives, does he describe it as arrival and recognition, or as one more adventure while keeping the money-losing cab show? The evidence record gains a claim for this passage (class interpretation, durability unresolved) whose review_trigger names the dated catalysts: next Emmy nominations (July 2027), any TV/film/streaming deal, his first public account of the 2026 loss, and Keep the Meter Running being sponsored, sold, made profitable or ended. The C34/C95 triggers also say that such a change requires re-checking the costly-choice argument, not just the fact.

findings.problem: The FAQ answers a present-tense award question with a flat "No." The show is ongoing (C102), it has YouTube's backing, and the category recurs every year, so a later nomination or win would make this metadata false. Search features could show it in a rich result long after the body is refreshed. The supporting claims (C40, C109) are marked stable with empty review_triggers, which goes against the standard's rule that changing figures be recorded as time_sensitive with an actionable trigger.
findings.acceptance_test: Either the question is anchored to 2026 (e.g. "Was SubwayTakes nominated for an Emmy?" or "Did SubwayTakes win the 2026 Emmy?") and the answer opens with the dated fact rather than a bare "No.", or the claims behind the FAQ are recorded as time_sensitive with review_trigger "Re-check each July Emmy nominations announcement and each September Creative Arts ceremony; update the FAQ and keywords if SubwayTakes or Rahma is nominated or wins." Preferably both. The body's dated sentences need no change.

C37 is re-recorded as time_sensitive with review_trigger: "Revisit the type argument when Kuo, Rahma's wife, a longtime collaborator or a reported profile quoting people close to him describes his temperament or motives on record."

assessment: Five-year test: the thesis passes. With every 2026 item removed (Emmy nomination and loss, Rolling Stone No. 11, Awards Radar, the Povich interview, the relaunched cab episodes), the Seven case still stands: the 2007 Monday, the 2024 airplane-ride passage, fun as the "number one" rule (2025), "talent has a very fun job" (2025) and the money-losing cab show (2022-2024). The Three case loses some 2026 support but remains fair. Date discipline is unusually good: nearly every event and quote carries a year or month, with no relative "recently" or "this year". Title, meta_title, persona_title and description are built on his own durable phrases. "The SubwayTakes host" stays an accurate identifier even if the show ends, and C102's trigger covers that case. The weaknesses are in tracking, not prose. The forward test that could flip a contested medium-confidence read has no observable split and no review trigger (future-F1). One FAQ answers a recurring-award question with a bare "No." (future-F2). Three changing positions or record-state claims are recorded as stable (future-F3 to F5). Existing triggers on the Harris dispute (C23/C80/C81), faith (C39), relationship status (C36) and the two series (C34/C95/C102) are actionable. Trimming the 2026 news layer (Rolling Stone ranking, the $4,100 title, Damascus) costs the thesis nothing if the editor needs words. Keep at least one 2026 cab-show beat, though, because it tests the closing quote. Similarity advisory: the tripped Tyla pair shares only the phrase "the pattern runs", with different arguments, and the other pairs share no phrases, so there is no meaningful reuse. The plain-steps Seven mechanism paragraph overlaps in substance with Travis-Kelce's general Seven description. It is ordinary type vocabulary and ties to Rahma in the next line, so no finding. Not a standard-format open case; eligibility does not apply.
